study type: Retrospective case control pilot study & prospective case control study
outcome: Presence of memory Treg (CD45RO+) in the fetus
cohort: Pregnant women with and without prior uterine scars from c-sections
finding: Fetuses born to mothers with prior uterine scars from c-sections and placental implantation over the scar had a five times higher maternal-fetal microchimerism and presence of memory Treg (CD45RO+) in the fetus.
mod_finding: Uterine scars from prior c-sections were associated with increased fetal antigen exposure and presence of memory Treg (CD45RO+) in the fetus.
